evidence: order-item.interface.ts: declares only IOrderItem (productId, quantity, unitPrice, lineTotal...), which is the line-item shape of the Order aggregate

order.interface.ts: IOrder uses `items: IOrderItem[]` and `shippingAddress: IShippingAddress`; IOrderEditable uses `shippingAddress: IShippingAddressEditable`, so it reuses the existing interfaces instead of copying their fields
shipping-address.interface.ts: `IShippingAddress extends IShippingAddressEditable` adds only `id`, so the address fields are declared in one place
Graph: Order, OrderItem and ShippingAddress implement IOrder, IOrderItem and IShippingAddress respectively, so all three interfaces back one aggregate
Minor: order.interface.ts has a header comment with the old path 'src/modules/orders/domain/interfaces/order.interface.ts'; this is a documentation issue, not a problem with cohesion
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files cover a single concern: the data shapes of the Order aggregate, meaning the order, its line items and its shipping address. order.interface.ts builds IOrder and IOrderEditable from IOrderItem and the shipping-address interfaces instead of redefining their fields. Address fields are declared only once, in IShippingAddressEditable, and IShippingAddress extends it with an id. IOrderEditable follows the same pattern by reusing IShippingAddressEditable. No rule or invariant is repeated: the totals fields (lineTotal, subtotal, totalPrice) are only declared, and no file computes them. No file goes around the module's own abstractions. Two small points don't change the result. IOrderItem has no 'Editable' variant, unlike the order and address interfaces. And the header comment in order.interface.ts gives an old path (src/modules/orders/domain/interfaces/...) instead of the real location under core/domain. Import paths are out of scope.
